hypothesis: In some types of non-Alzheimer's, non-aged human brain cells, APOE4 disruption of lipid metabolism, compared with APOE3, results in impaired late endosome/lysosome function.

paper.title: ApoE4-dependent lysosomal cholesterol accumulation impairs mitochondrial homeostasis and oxidative phosphorylation in human astrocytes.

findings.finding_description: Filipin III cholesterol staining co-labeled with LysoTracker showed significant cholesterol accumulation in ApoE4 compared with isogenic ApoE3 iPSC-derived astrocytes, mainly within lysosomes. This links APOE4-driven lipid disruption to a lysosomal storage phenotype. The main pair comes from an 87-year-old sporadic AD donor, but the cells are reprogrammed iPSC derivatives.
findings.quote: As previously reported,5,17 we found a significant accumulation of cholesterol in ApoE4 astrocytes compared with ApoE3 astrocytes (Figures 4A and 4B), which was predominantly observed in lysosomes (Figures 4A and 4C).
findings.summary: ApoE4 astrocytes accumulate cholesterol predominantly in lysosomes vs isogenic ApoE3.

findings.finding_description: Tandem RFP-GFP-LC3 reporter showed more autophagosomes (RFP+GFP+) and fewer autolysosomes (RFP-only) in ApoE4 than ApoE3 astrocytes. This indicates impaired autophagic flux, a surrogate for defective lysosomal degradation.
findings.quote: We observed increased autophagosomes (RFP and GFP) and decreased autolysosomes (RFP only) in ApoE4 astrocytes compared with ApoE3 astrocytes, indicating impaired autophagy flux (Figures 3L–3O).
findings.summary: ApoE4 astrocytes show impaired autophagic flux by tfLC3 reporter.

findings.finding_description: Methyl-β-cyclodextrin (100 μM, 4 days) treatment of ApoE4 astrocytes restored autolysosome and autophagosome areas, normalizing autophagic flux. Cholesterol depletion is a surrogate perturbation of APOE4 lipid disruption; flux is a surrogate of lysosomal function.
findings.quote: We observed the restoration of autolysosomes and autophagosome areas in ApoE4 astrocytes with MβCD treatment, suggesting normalized autophagy flux (Figures 5A–5D).
findings.summary: Cholesterol depletion rescues autophagic flux in ApoE4 astrocytes.
findings.experimental_system: Human iPSC-derived ApoE4 astrocytes treated with MβCD vs ApoE3

findings.finding_description: In a second isogenic pair (healthy-donor background), ApoE4 astrocytes again showed impaired autophagic flux vs ApoE3, and MβCD treatment attenuated it. This replicates the result in a non-AD donor background, though the donor was aged 75.
findings.quote: As shown in Figures 3L–3O, ApoE4 astrocytes displayed impaired autophagy flux compared with their isogenic ApoE3 cells, and this effect was attenuated by MβCD treatment (Figures S6F–S6I).
findings.summary: Impaired flux and MβCD rescue replicated in a second (healthy-donor) isogenic pair.
findings.experimental_system: Second isogenic ApoE3/ApoE4 human iPSC-derived astrocyte pair (healthy donor AG09173)

findings.finding_description: Cathepsin B activity was about 50% higher in ApoE4 than in ApoE3 astrocytes. The authors read this as lysosomal dysregulation, but higher protease activity does not by itself indicate impaired lysosomal function and partly argues against it.
findings.quote: Consistent with LysoTracker staining, ApoE4 astrocytes displayed an approximately 50% increase in cathepsin B activity compared with ApoE3 astrocytes (Figure 3H).
findings.summary: ApoE4 increases (not decreases) lysosomal cathepsin B activity by ~50%.

findings.finding_description: p62 and LC3 immunostaining were both significantly increased in ApoE4 astrocytes. This suggests autophagosome accumulation from impaired autolysosomal degradation.
findings.quote: We observed that both p62 and LC3 levels were significantly increased in ApoE4 astrocytes compared with those in ApoE3 astrocytes (Figures 3I–3K)
findings.summary: ApoE4 astrocytes accumulate p62 and LC3.

findings.finding_description: LysoTracker/MitoTracker staining showed increased lysosomal area, unchanged mitochondrial area, and increased lysosome-mitochondria colocalization in ApoE4 astrocytes. The authors interpret this as impaired lysosome-dependent mitochondrial degradation.
findings.quote: We repeatedly observed an increased lysosomal area, although the mitochondrial area was indistinguishable in ApoE4 astrocytes compared with ApoE3 cells (Figures 3A–3C). The significantly increased colocalization of lysosomes and mitochondria found in ApoE4 astrocytes was likely due to lysosomal dysfunction
findings.summary: ApoE4 increases lysosomal area and lysosome-mitochondria colocalization.

findings.finding_description: Individual lysosomes were larger, and LysoTracker intensity higher, in ApoE4 astrocytes. The authors treat LysoTracker intensity as positively associated with lysosomal activity.
findings.quote: We observed an increase in the size of lysosomes in ApoE4 astrocytes (Figures 3E and 3F). We also observed that ApoE4 increased the intensity of LysoTracker, which is positively associated with lysosomal activity (Figure 3G).
findings.summary: ApoE4 enlarges lysosomes and increases LysoTracker intensity.

findings.finding_description: MβCD (100 μM, 4 days) reduced lysosomal cholesterol in ApoE4 astrocytes and normalized LysoTracker area and intensity toward ApoE3 levels. ToF-SIMS showed plasma membrane lipids were not disrupted.
findings.quote: We further observed restoration of lysosomal activity, as indicated by the mitigated intensity of LysoTracker after lysosomal cholesterol depletion (Figures 4D and 4F).
findings.summary: Cholesterol depletion normalizes lysosomal cholesterol and LysoTracker phenotypes in ApoE4 astrocytes.
findings.experimental_system: Human iPSC-derived ApoE4 astrocytes treated with MβCD

findings.finding_description: Simvastatin, an independent cholesterol-lowering perturbation, normalized ApoE4-dependent increases in lysosomal cholesterol and LysoTracker-positive area in astrocytes.
findings.quote: Simvastatin treatment also normalized ApoE4-dependent increases in lysosomal cholesterol accumulation and LysoTracker-positive areas in astrocytes (Figures 4G–4I).
findings.summary: Statin normalizes lysosomal cholesterol and LysoTracker area in ApoE4 astrocytes.
findings.experimental_system: Human iPSC-derived ApoE4 astrocytes treated with simvastatin

findings.finding_description: Proteomics identified 254 down- and 238 upregulated proteins in ApoE4 vs ApoE3 astrocytes, with significant subsets restored by short-term MβCD. Pathway analysis indicated normalization of autophagy and protein degradation pathways.
findings.quote: Many of these pathways, including those related to autophagy and protein degradation, were normalized by MβCD treatment (Figure 6B).
findings.summary: MβCD normalizes ApoE4-altered autophagy/protein degradation proteome pathways.
findings.experimental_system: Human iPSC-derived ApoE3, ApoE4, and MβCD-treated ApoE4 astrocytes (LFQ proteomics)

findings.finding_description: Electron microscopy showed enlarged, more circular, less complex mitochondria in ApoE4 astrocytes, all restored by MβCD. This is a downstream readout consistent with failed lysosome-dependent mitochondrial clearance; it does not measure lysosomes directly.
findings.quote: All mitochondrial structural abnormalities observed in ApoE4 astrocytes were completely restored by MβCD treatment (Figures 5E–5J).
findings.summary: Cholesterol depletion restores ApoE4-associated mitochondrial morphology defects.
findings.experimental_system: Human iPSC-derived ApoE3/ApoE4 astrocytes ± MβCD, TEM
